title: Personal Selling Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 30
description:
Arjun wants one more shop for Laddoo Lab: the busiest one, right next to a big school. But the owner, Mr. Shetty, says no to almost every new brand. A poster won't change his mind. A person might. In this animated lesson we use Laddoo Lab, a millet laddoo brand from Bengaluru, to understand personal selling.

You will see Philip Kotler and Gary Armstrong's definition of personal selling (making sales and building customer relationships), and then watch Arjun walk through their seven steps live: prospecting and qualifying, the pre-approach, the approach, the presentation, handling objections, closing and follow-up, while Mr. Shetty's interest rises, dips at his worry, and turns into a yes. We see why a person can beat an ad (two-way talk, a tailored pitch and trust), and how prospecting, presentation, handling objections and follow-up work today at a bank, a phone store, a car showroom and an insurance agent. We also look at the human side honestly: personal selling is slow and costly (Kotler and Armstrong call it the most expensive promotion tool per contact), some salespeople push too hard, and Zoya stops Arjun from promising more than is true.

This is Episode 30 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
